ja: だいさんじゅういちかい

p.src: When Xiren saw the fresh blood she had coughed up on the floor, her heart went cold. She remembered often hearing people say, “When the young cough blood, they cannot count on many years; even if they live long, they will be invalids for the rest of their lives.” At the thought of these words, all her cherished hopes of attaining honor and distinction in the future turned to ashes, and tears began to fall from her eyes. Seeing her cry, Baoyu too felt a pang of sorrow and asked, “How do you feel?” Forcing a smile, Xiren replied, “I’m perfectly well. What should I feel?” Baoyu wanted at once to have someone warm yellow wine and fetch some Goat’s-Blood Lidong Pills. Xiren took his hand and said with a smile, “If you make such a commotion, you’ll stir up ever so many people, and they’ll blame me for behaving frivolously. No one knows of it now; if your fuss lets everyone find out, it will reflect badly on both you and me. The sensible thing is to send a boy tomorrow to ask Imperial Physician Wang about it and get a little medicine; then I shall soon be well. Wouldn’t it be better to do it without anyone being the wiser?” Baoyu saw the sense in this and had no choice but to desist. He poured tea from the table and gave it to Xiren to rinse her mouth. Xiren knew that Baoyu was uneasy. If she told him not to wait on her, he would certainly refuse, and besides, they were sure to alarm the others. It seemed best to let him do as he pleased; so she remained on the couch and allowed Baoyu to tend her. As soon as the fifth watch began, Baoyu did not even stop to wash or comb his hair, but hurriedly dressed, went out, summoned Wang Jiren, and questioned him personally and in detail. Wang Jiren asked how it had happened and, finding that it was merely an injury, gave him the name of a pill and explained how it should be taken and how it should be applied externally. Baoyu committed the instructions to memory, returned to the Garden, and treated her according to the prescription. But no more need be said of this.

p.src: That day was the joyous Dragon Boat Festival: calamus and mugwort adorned the doors, and tiger charms were tied around people’s arms. At noon, Lady Wang prepared a feast and invited Aunt Xue, her daughter, and the others to celebrate the festival meal. Baoyu noticed that Baochai was distant and would not speak to him, and knew it was because of what had happened the day before. Lady Wang saw that Baoyu looked listless and assumed that, after the incident with Jinchuan the previous day, he was too ashamed to face her; she therefore ignored him all the more. Lin Daiyu, seeing Baoyu so dispirited, supposed that he felt ill at ease because he had offended Baochai; consequently, she too became listless in manner. Lady Wang had told Xifeng the previous evening about the affair involving Baoyu and Jinchuan. Knowing that Lady Wang was upset, Xifeng hardly dared to joke or laugh, but took her cue from Lady Wang’s expression and behaved with still greater reserve. When Jia Yingchun and her sisters saw that no one was enjoying the occasion, they too lost all interest in it. And so, after sitting together for a short while, they all dispersed.

p.src: By nature, Lin Daiyu preferred parting to gathering. Her view had a certain logic to it. She would say, “Whenever people come together, they must eventually part. If gathering is joyful, will it not be desolate when the time comes to part? And since desolation brings sorrow, it would be better never to gather at all. In the same way, flowers inspire love when they bloom, but deepen melancholy when they fade; therefore, it would be better if they never bloomed.” Thus, when others found cause for joy, she instead found cause for sorrow. Baoyu’s temperament was just the opposite: he wished everyone could always remain together, fearing that any sudden parting would bring sorrow; he wished flowers could remain forever in bloom, fearing that if they suddenly faded, all delight would be lost. Yet once the feast had ended and the flowers had fallen, no matter how boundless his grief, there was nothing he could do. Consequently, when today’s company broke up in low spirits, Lin Daiyu was not particularly affected; Baoyu, however, grew depressed and unhappy, and returned to his room sighing again and again. Just then Qingwen came to change his clothes, and as ill luck would have it, she let a fan slip from her hand. It fell to the floor and one of its ribs snapped. Baoyu exclaimed with a sigh, “What a fool! What a fool! What will ever become of you? When you have a household and affairs of your own to manage one day, will you still act so heedlessly, with no thought for the consequences?” Qingwen sneered. “Second Master has developed quite a temper lately. At the slightest thing, you give us a black look. The other day you even struck Xiren, and today you’re finding fault with us again. If you want to kick or beat me, do as you please. Dropping a fan is an ordinary enough mishap. In the past, no one knows how many glass jars and agate bowls of that sort were broken, yet we never heard you breathe a word of anger. And now you make such a fuss over a single fan. Why make such trouble over it? If you dislike us, send us away and choose better servants to wait on you. Wouldn’t it be better for us to part on good terms?” Hearing this, Baoyu shook all over with rage and said, “There is no need to be so impatient. The day will come when we part!”

p.src: Xiren had already heard everything from the other side and hurried over to ask Baoyu, “Everything was fine—what has happened now? Just as I always say: ‘The moment I am not here, something goes wrong.’” Qingwen gave a cold laugh. “Since you know so well what to say, Sister, you should have come sooner and spared Master all this anger. Since time immemorial, you alone have waited upon him; plainly none of us has ever served him at all. You serve him so well that only yesterday you earned a kick in the ribs. As for those of us who cannot serve him properly, who knows what punishment awaits us tomorrow!” These words left Xiren both angry and ashamed. She was about to answer, but when she saw that Baoyu’s face had gone yellow with rage, she had no choice but to restrain herself. Nudging Qingwen, she said, “There, dear sister, go outside and take a stroll. It was our fault.” When Qingwen heard her say “our,” naturally meaning herself and Baoyu, jealousy sharpened her anger. She laughed coldly several times and said, “I should like to know just who this ‘we’ is. Do not make me blush on your behalf! Even that secret business you two carried on cannot be hidden from me. What gives you the right to call yourselves ‘we’ already? Properly and openly, you have not even earned the position of a concubine yet. You are still only the same as I am, so how can you call yourselves ‘we’?” Xiren’s face swelled dark purple with shame. On reflection, she realized that she had indeed misspoken. Meanwhile Baoyu said, “Since you are all so resentful, tomorrow I shall make a special point of raising her position.” Xiren hastily took Baoyu’s hand. “She is a foolish girl. Why argue with her? Besides, you are usually so forbearing. You have let far worse things pass—what is wrong with you today?” Qingwen sneered. “I am a fool, of course. Who would deign to speak to me?” Hearing this, Xiren said, “Are you quarrelling with me, miss, or with Second Master? If you are angry with me, say it to me alone; there is no need to quarrel in front of Second Master. If you are angry with him, you should not make such a commotion that everyone hears of it. I only came in because of the trouble, hoping to separate you and keep everyone from harm. Yet you have turned on me instead. You seem angry neither with me nor with Second Master, yet every word carries a hidden barb. What, in the end, do you mean by it? I shall say no more. You may have your say.” With that, she turned to leave. Baoyu said to Qingwen, “There is no need for you to be angry. I think I understand what is on your mind. I shall tell Madam that you are grown now and ask her to send you away. Would that suit you?” At these words Qingwen grew heartsore again and said through her tears, “Why should I leave? If you have tired of me, you may devise whatever means you like to send me away, but you will not succeed.”

p.src: Baoyu said, “When have I ever had to endure such quarrelling? You must be determined to leave. I had better tell Madam and have her send you away.” As he spoke, he rose to go. Xiren hurried back to bar his way and asked with a smile, “Where are you going?” “To tell Madam,” said Baoyu. Xiren laughed. “How absurd! If you truly go and report this, will you not be ashamed of yourself? Even if she genuinely wants to go, you should wait until her anger has subsided and then mention it casually to Madam. It will not be too late. If you rush to report it now as though it were some grave affair, will that not make Madam suspicious?” “Madam will not be suspicious,” said Baoyu. “I shall tell her plainly that Qingwen made a scene because she wanted to leave.” Qingwen cried, “When did I ever make a scene about wanting to leave? Even in your anger, you should not pin such words on me. Go and report me if you like. I would sooner dash my head against the wall and die than pass through this door.” Baoyu said, “Now that is strange. If you will not leave, what are you making all this trouble for? I cannot bear such quarrelling. It would be cleaner and simpler if you left.” With that, he insisted upon going to report the matter. Seeing that she could not stop him, Xiren had no choice but to kneel down. Bihen, Qiuwen, Sheyue, and the other maids had heard the quarrel and were waiting outside in utter silence to see what would happen. Now, hearing Xiren kneel and plead with him, they all came in and knelt together. Baoyu hastily helped Xiren to her feet, sighed, and sat down on the bed. After telling the others to rise, he said to Xiren, “What would you have me do? I may wear my heart to pieces, yet no one understands.” As he spoke, tears began to fall despite himself. When Xiren saw Baoyu weeping, she too began to cry.

p.src: Qingwen stood to one side weeping and was just about to speak when Lin Daiyu entered, so she went out. Lin Daiyu asked with a smile, “Why are you crying like this in the middle of a great festival? Surely you have not quarrelled over who should eat the rice dumplings?” Baoyu and Xiren both burst out laughing. Daiyu said, “If Second Brother will not tell me, I need only ask you to learn the truth.” As she spoke, she patted Xiren on the shoulder and said with a smile, “Dear sister-in-law, tell me. You two must have had a quarrel. Tell your little sister, and I shall make peace between you.” Xiren pushed her away. “Miss Lin, why must you tease me? I am only a maid, yet you insist on talking nonsense.” Daiyu laughed. “You may call yourself a maid, but I treat you only as my sister-in-law.” Baoyu said, “Why must you bring such a scandalous name upon her? Even as things stand, people gossip about her. How can she bear your saying such things too?” Xiren said with a rueful smile, “Miss Lin, you do not know what is in my heart. Unless I were to stop breathing and die, there is no release for me.” Lin Daiyu laughed. “If you died, I cannot say what anyone else might do, but I would be the first to cry myself to death.” Baoyu laughed. “If you die, I shall become a monk.” Xiren laughed. “Do behave yourself. Why must you say such things again?” Lin Daiyu held up two fingers, pursed her lips, and laughed. “That makes two vows to become a monk. From now on, I shall keep count of every time you promise to take the tonsure.” Hearing this, Baoyu knew that she was alluding to what he had said before. He merely smiled and let the matter drop.

p.src: After Daiyu had gone, someone soon came to say, “Master Xue invites you,” so Baoyu had no choice but to go. It turned out to be a drinking party, and since he could not decline, he had to remain until the feast ended. When he returned that evening, he was somewhat tipsy. Staggering into his own courtyard, he saw that the couch and pillows for enjoying the cool air had already been set out, and someone lay asleep upon the couch. Taking her for Xiren, Baoyu sat down on the edge of the couch, nudged her, and asked, “Does it hurt less now?” The sleeper turned over, sat up, and said, “Why must you come and provoke me again?” Baoyu looked and saw that it was not Xiren after all, but Qingwen. Baoyu took her by the hand, pulled her down beside him, and said with a smile, “You are growing more spoiled and wilful by the day. This morning you dropped and broke a fan, and merely because I said a couple of words, you answered me with all those things. It would have been one thing to speak so to me, but when Xiren came with the best intentions to reason with you, you dragged her into it as well. Think for yourself—was that right?” Qingwen replied, “It is stiflingly hot—why must you keep tugging at me? What would it look like if someone came and saw us? Someone like me is not fit to sit here anyway.” Baoyu laughed. “If you know you are not fit to sit here, why were you sleeping here?” Qingwen had no answer and burst out laughing again. “It would have been all right if you had not come. It became improper only when you arrived. Now get up and let me go and bathe. Xiren and Sheyue have both bathed already. I will call them to attend you.” Baoyu said with a smile, “I have just drunk a good deal more wine, so I need another wash. Since you have not bathed yet, fetch some water and we will bathe together.” Qingwen waved her hand and laughed. “No, no! I would not dare court trouble with you, young master. I still remember when Bihen attended you in the bath: it took a good four or six hours, and goodness knows what the two of you were doing. None of us could very well go inside. When at last you had finished and we went in to look, the floor was so flooded that the water covered the legs of the bed, and even the mat had pools standing on it. None of us could imagine how you had managed to bathe, and we laughed about it for days. I have no time to clean up such a mess, so do not ask me to bathe with you. It is cool today anyway, and since you bathed earlier, you need not do so again. I will draw a basin of water instead, so that you can wash your face and comb out your hair. Yuanyang has just sent over a great quantity of fruit, all chilling in that crystal jar. I will have them serve you some.” Baoyu laughed. “In that case, you are not allowed to go and bathe either. Just wash your hands and bring the fruit so we can eat it.” Qingwen smiled. “I am so careless that I even dropped and broke a fan. How could I possibly be worthy of serving fruit? If I should break another plate, it would be more dreadful still.” Baoyu laughed. “Break them if you like. Such things exist only for people to use. You like one thing and I another; everyone has a different nature.

p.src: Take a fan: it is meant for fanning, but if you want to tear it up for amusement, that is perfectly all right. You must simply never take your anger out on it. Likewise, cups and plates are meant to hold things, but if you enjoy the sound they make, you may deliberately smash them. Just do not use them to vent your anger. That is what it means to cherish things.” Hearing this, Qingwen laughed. “If that is what you say, then bring me a fan and let me tear it. There is nothing I enjoy more than tearing things.” Baoyu laughed and handed her his fan. Qingwen took it and, sure enough, tore it in two with a sharp rip; several more ripping sounds followed. Baoyu stood beside her, laughing. “What a fine sound! Tear it louder!” As he spoke, Sheyue came over and said with a smile, “Try to commit a little less wickedness.” Baoyu ran up to her, snatched the fan from her hand, and gave it to Qingwen as well. Qingwen took it and tore it into several pieces, and she and Baoyu both burst into laughter. Sheyue protested, “What is the meaning of this? Must you amuse yourselves with my belongings?” Baoyu laughed. “Open the fan case and choose another for yourself. p.src: Do you remember how, in the third or fourth month of last year, while she was staying here, she put on Brother Bao’s robe and boots and tied his headband around her brow? At a sudden glance she looked just like Brother Bao, except for the two extra earrings. She stood behind that chair and fooled the Old Lady into calling again and again, ‘Baoyu, come over here. Mind that the tassel on the lamp above you doesn’t shake dust into your eyes.’ She only laughed and would not go over. At last none of us could hold back our laughter. Only then did the Old Lady laugh too and say, ‘Why, you look prettier dressed as a boy!’” “That was nothing,” said Lin Daiyu. “The best was when she came here in the first month of the year before last. She had been here only a couple of days when it snowed. That day the Old Lady and Aunt had apparently just returned from paying homage before the ancestral portraits, and one of the Old Lady’s brand-new bright-red orangutan-felt cloaks had been left lying there. The moment no one was watching, she put it on. It was much too large and long, so she tied a handkerchief around her waist and went with the maids to make snow figures in the back courtyard. Then she took a tumble by the edge of the ditch and covered herself in muddy water.” As she spoke, everyone remembered the incident and laughed. Baochai smiled and asked Nanny Zhou, “Mamma Zhou, is your young lady still as mischievous as ever?” Nanny Zhou laughed too. “I could put up with her mischief,” Yingchun said with a smile. “What bothers me is how much she talks. Even when she is lying in bed, she chatters on and on, laughing for a while and talking for a while. I cannot imagine where she finds so much to say.” “Perhaps she has improved by now,” said Lady Wang. “The other day a family came to look her over as a prospective bride, and she will plainly have a husband’s family before long. Surely she cannot still behave like that.” Grandmother Jia then asked, “Will she be staying today, or is she going home?” Nanny Zhou replied with a smile, “Didn’t you notice, Old Lady, that she brought her clothes with her? Of course she will stay for a couple of days.” “Isn’t Brother Baoyu at home?” Shi Xiangyun asked. Baochai laughed. “She thinks of no one else, only Brother Bao. What a pair of silly children they are! That proves she has not outgrown her mischief.” “You are grown up now,” said Grandmother Jia. “You must stop calling one another by childhood names.” No sooner had she spoken than Baoyu came in and said with a smile, “Sister Yun, you are here! Why didn’t you come the other day when we sent someone to fetch you?” “The Old Lady has only just spoken of this,” said Lady Wang, “and here he comes calling her by name again.” “Your brother has something nice waiting for you,” said Lin Daiyu. “What nice thing?” asked Shi Xiangyun. Baoyu laughed. “Don’t believe her! I haven’t seen you for only a few days, yet you have grown taller again.” Xiangyun asked with a smile, “Is Sister Xiren well?” “Thank you for remembering her,” replied Baoyu.

p.src: “I have brought her something nice,” said Xiangyun. As she spoke, she took out a handkerchief tied into a bundle. “What could it be?” asked Baoyu. “You might better have brought her a couple of those carnelian rings you sent us the other day.” “Then what do you think this is?” Xiangyun asked with a laugh. With that, she opened it. When everyone looked, they saw that it was indeed a packet of four of the same carnelian rings she had sent last time. Lin Daiyu laughed. “Just look at the way she goes about things! The other day, when you sent identical rings to all of us, wouldn’t it have saved trouble simply to include theirs then? Yet today you have gone to all the trouble of bringing them yourself. I thought it must be some new curiosity, but it turns out to be the very same thing. You truly are a muddlehead.” “You are the muddlehead!” Shi Xiangyun retorted with a laugh. “Let me explain my reasoning, and everyone can judge which of us is muddled. When I send presents to you young ladies, the messenger need not say a word; as soon as they are carried in, everyone naturally knows they are meant for you. But if I sent things for your maids, I would first have to tell the messenger which one was for this maid and which for that. It would be all right if the messenger understood clearly, but if he were a little muddleheaded and could not even remember the maids’ names, he would babble nonsense and end up confusing your presents as well. It would not have mattered if I had sent a woman who knew the household well, but the other day they happened to send a young male servant. How could I tell him all the maids’ names? Since I was coming anyway, wasn’t it clearer for me to bring the rings to them myself?” As she spoke, she set down the four rings and said, “One is for Sister Xiren, one for Sister Yuanyang, one for Sister Jinchuan, and one for Sister Ping’er. They are meant for four different people—could the young servants possibly have remembered all that so clearly?” Everyone laughed on hearing this and said, “That is perfectly sensible.” Baoyu laughed. “You are still as quick-tongued as ever and never yield to anyone.” On hearing this, Lin Daiyu gave a cold laugh. “She may not know how to talk, but her golden qilin does.” With that, she rose and left. Fortunately, none of the others had heard her; only Xue Baochai pursed her lips in a smile. Baoyu had heard her, however, and regretted having said the wrong thing yet again. Then, seeing Baochai smile, he could not help smiling too. When Baochai saw Baoyu smile, she hurriedly rose and went away to find Lin Daiyu and talk with her.

p.src: Grandmother Jia said to Xiangyun, “After your tea, rest awhile, then go and see your sisters-in-law. It is cool in the Garden too, so go for a stroll with your cousins.” Xiangyun agreed. She wrapped up the three rings and, after resting awhile, rose to visit Xifeng and the others. Her nurses and maids followed her. At Xifeng’s quarters she chatted and laughed for a while, then entered Prospect Garden, paid her respects to Li Gongcai, sat briefly, and went on to Happy Red Court to find Xiren. Turning to her attendants, she said, “You need not follow me. Go and visit your own friends and relations; just leave Cuilü here to wait on me.” At this, they went off to seek out their aunts and sisters-in-law, and soon only Xiangyun and Cuilü remained. Cuilü asked, “Why haven’t these lotuses bloomed yet?” “It isn’t time yet,” said Shi Xiangyun. Cuilü said, “Are they like the ones in our pond—double-flowered lotuses too?” “These aren’t as fine as ours,” said Xiangyun. Cuilü said, “Over there they have a pomegranate tree with four or five blossoms joined together, one tier rising above another. It’s a wonder the tree can grow them.” Shi Xiangyun said, “Flowers and plants are just like people: when their vital energies are abundant, they flourish.” Cuilü turned her face aside. “I don’t believe that. If they’re like people, why have I never seen anyone grow another head atop the first?” Xiangyun could not help laughing. “I tell you to hold your tongue, yet you insist on talking. How is anyone supposed to answer that? Everything between heaven and earth is born endowed with the twin forces of yin and yang. Whether normal or perverse, ordinary or strange, all the myriad transformations arise from the harmony or opposition of yin and yang. When something is born that few people have seen, they call it extraordinary, but the underlying principle is still the same.” Cuilü asked, “Then from the creation of heaven and earth down to the present, has everything always been yin and yang?” Xiangyun laughed. “You little fool, the more you talk, the more nonsense you spout. What do you mean, ‘everything is yin and yang’? Do you imagine yin and yang are separate objects? Though ‘yin’ and ‘yang’ are written as two words, they are one principle: when yang reaches its limit it becomes yin, and when yin reaches its limit it becomes yang. It is not that, when yin is exhausted, some new yang is born, or that, when yang is exhausted, some new yin is born.” Cuilü said, “Now I’m utterly confused! What exactly are yin and yang? They have neither shape nor shadow. I only want to ask you, miss: what do yin and yang look like?” Xiangyun replied, “How could yin and yang have any particular appearance? They are merely vital forces, which take form when embodied in things. For instance, heaven is yang and earth is yin; water is yin and fire is yang; the sun is yang and the moon is yin.” Hearing this, Cuilü laughed. “Yes, yes, now I finally understand.

p.src: No wonder everyone calls the sun the ‘Great Yang,’ while fortune-tellers call the moon the ‘Great Yin Star.’ That is the reason.” Xiangyun laughed. “Amitabha! At last you understand.” Cuilü said, “I can accept that great things like those have yin and yang, but surely mosquitoes, fleas, gnats, flowers, grasses, tiles, and bricks don’t have yin and yang too?” Xiangyun replied, “How could anything be without yin and yang? Even a single leaf has yin and yang: the upper side facing the sunlight is yang, while the shaded underside is yin.” Cuilü nodded and laughed. “So that’s how it is. Now I understand. But what about the fan in my hand—which side is yang and which is yin?” Xiangyun said, “The front on this side is yang, and the back on the other side is yin.” Cuilü nodded and laughed again. She wanted to ask about several more things but could not think of any. Then, suddenly lowering her eyes, she noticed the golden qilin tied to Xiangyun’s girdle. Lifting it, she asked, “Miss, does this have yin and yang too?” Xiangyun replied, “Among beasts and birds, the male is yang and the female is yin; females are yin and males are yang. How could it not?” Cuilü asked, “Then is this one male or female?” “Even I don’t know that,” said Xiangyun. Cuilü said, “Never mind that. But if everything has yin and yang, why is it that we human beings don’t?” Xiangyun spat playfully in her face. “Shameless creature! Just mind where you’re going! Your questions grow more improper every moment!” Cuilü laughed. “Why shouldn’t you tell me? I know the answer anyway, so you needn’t try to stump me.” Xiangyun laughed. “What do you know?” Cuilü replied, “You, miss, are yang, and I am yin.” At this, Xiangyun covered her mouth with her handkerchief and burst into peals of laughter. Cuilü said, “I got it right, and that’s why you’re laughing so.” “Quite right, quite right,” said Xiangyun. Cuilü said, “By the rules governing people, masters are yang and servants are yin. Do you think I don’t understand even that great principle?” Xiangyun laughed. “You understand it very well indeed.” Talking as they walked, they had just reached the rose trellis when Xiangyun said, “Look! Someone has dropped a piece of jewelry. See how it glitters there.” Cuilü hurried over, picked it up, and clasped it in her hand. Laughing, she said, “Now we can tell which is yin and which is yang.” As she spoke, she first examined Shi Xiangyun’s qilin. Xiangyun wanted to see what she had found, but Cuilü stubbornly refused to let go of it. Laughing, she said, “It is a treasure, so you may not see it, miss. Where could this have come from? How extraordinary!”

Let us go together.”
With that, they all entered Happy Red Court.

Xiren was leaning against the railing below the steps, enjoying the breeze. When she suddenly saw Xiangyun, she hurried down to welcome her, took her by the hand, and smilingly exchanged news after their long separation.
Presently they went inside and sat down. Baoyu smiled and said, “You should have come sooner. I found something wonderful and have been saving it especially for you.”
As he spoke, he felt about in his clothes. After searching for some time, he cried, “Oh!” and asked Xiren, “Did you put that thing away?”
“What thing?” asked Xiren.
“The qilin I got the other day,” said Baoyu.
Xiren said, “You carry it with you every day. Why ask me?”
At this, Baoyu clapped his hands and exclaimed, “Then I’ve lost it! Where am I to look for it now?”
He was about to rise and search for it himself.
Only then did Xiangyun realize that he had dropped it. She asked with a smile, “Since when have you had a qilin too?”
Baoyu replied, “I had quite a time getting it the other day. I have no idea when I lost it; I’m muddleheaded myself.”
Xiangyun laughed. “Fortunately it is only a trinket, yet see how flustered you are.”
As she spoke, she opened her hand. “Look—is this it?”
The moment Baoyu saw it, he could not contain his delight and said… What happened next is unknown; listen to the explanation in the following chapter.
